questions.question: What is the universal curved-arrow sequence in a single-step Brønsted acid-base reaction?

options.label: A
options.text: One arrow from the acidic proton to the base lone pair.

options.label: B
options.text: One arrow from the base lone pair to the acidic proton, and a second arrow from the H-A σ bond onto the conjugate base atom A.

options.label: C
options.text: Two arrows transferring protons in opposite directions simultaneously.

options.label: D
options.text: An arrow breaking the base into two ions.

questions.correct_answer: One arrow from the base lone pair to the acidic proton, and a second arrow from the H-A σ bond onto the conjugate base atom A.
questions.explanation: The electron pair of the base forms a new bond to H⁺, while the bonding pair in H-A is transferred entirely to atom A.

questions.topic: ARIO Atom Size Effect in Thiol vs Alcohol
questions.question: Why is ethanethiol (CH₃CH₂SH, pKa ~ 10.5) more acidic than ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH, pKa ~ 16) mechanistically?

options.label: A
options.text: The larger 3p orbital of sulfur delocalizes and stabilizes negative charge density over a larger volume than the compact 2p orbital of oxygen.

options.label: B
options.text: Ethanethiol undergoes rapid resonance delocalization into the ethyl chain.

options.label: C
options.text: Sulfur is more electronegative than oxygen on the Pauling scale.

options.label: D
options.text: Ethanol forms stronger intramolecular hydrogen bonds that trap the proton.

questions.correct_answer: The larger 3p orbital of sulfur delocalizes and stabilizes negative charge density over a larger volume than the compact 2p orbital of oxygen.
questions.explanation: Down a column in the periodic table, atomic size dominates over electronegativity: larger polarizable orbitals stabilize conjugate base anions.

questions.question: What mechanistic factor accounts for the ~11 pKa unit acidity difference between acetic acid (pKa 4.76) and ethanol (pKa 16)?

options.label: A
options.text: The acetate conjugate base delocalizes negative charge equally across two electronegative oxygen atoms via resonance, whereas ethoxide localizes charge on one oxygen.

options.label: B
options.text: Ethanol undergoes spontaneous homolytic cleavage in water.

options.label: C
options.text: Acetate anion is stabilized by aromaticity.

options.label: D
options.text: Acetic acid has stronger inductive electron donation from its methyl group.

questions.correct_answer: The acetate conjugate base delocalizes negative charge equally across two electronegative oxygen atoms via resonance, whereas ethoxide localizes charge on one oxygen.
questions.explanation: Resonance delocalization of the negative charge over two equivalent oxygen atoms provides massive stabilization to the carboxylate conjugate base.

questions.question: How does a trifluoromethyl group (-CF₃) mechanistically decrease the pKa of an adjacent carboxylic acid?

options.label: A
options.text: Fluorine forms covalent bonds directly with incoming hydronium ions.

options.label: B
options.text: Fluorine donates lone pairs into the carboxylate π system via resonance.

options.label: C
options.text: The CF₃ group acts as a Brønsted base that absorbs excess protons.

options.label: D
options.text: Strongly electronegative fluorine atoms pull σ-electron density through inductive polarization, dispersing negative charge away from the carboxylate group.

questions.correct_answer: Strongly electronegative fluorine atoms pull σ-electron density through inductive polarization, dispersing negative charge away from the carboxylate group.
questions.explanation: Inductive electron withdrawal through σ bonds stabilizes the conjugate base anion, lowering the energy barrier for proton loss.

questions.question: Why is acetylene (sp, pKa 25) significantly more acidic than ethylene (sp², pKa 44) and ethane (sp³, pKa 50)?

options.label: A
options.text: The sp orbital has a larger volume than sp³ orbitals.

options.label: B
options.text: Acetylene undergoes resonance delocalization upon losing a proton.

options.label: C
options.text: The sp hybrid orbital of the acetylide carbanion has 50% s-character, holding the lone pair electrons closer to the positively charged nucleus.

options.label: D
options.text: The triple bond creates an internal dipole that repels protons.

questions.correct_answer: The sp hybrid orbital of the acetylide carbanion has 50% s-character, holding the lone pair electrons closer to the positively charged nucleus.
questions.explanation: Higher s-character means electrons reside closer to the nucleus, significantly enhancing carbanion conjugate base stability.

questions.question: What is the mechanistic fate of sodium ethoxide (NaOEt) when added to pure water?

options.label: A
options.text: Ethoxide remains unreacted as free C₂H₅O⁻ ions.

options.label: B
options.text: Ethoxide decomposes to ethylene gas and water.

options.label: C
options.text: Ethoxide rapidly and quantitatively abstracts a proton from water to form ethanol and hydroxide ion (OH⁻), the strongest base that can exist in water.

options.label: D
options.text: Ethoxide is oxidized to acetic acid by dissolved oxygen.

questions.correct_answer: Ethoxide rapidly and quantitatively abstracts a proton from water to form ethanol and hydroxide ion (OH⁻), the strongest base that can exist in water.
questions.explanation: Any base stronger than hydroxide is leveled by water, converting completely to the solvent's conjugate base (OH⁻).

questions.question: What is the first elementary step when AlCl₃ reacts with 2-chloro-2-methylpropane?

options.label: A
options.text: A chlorine lone pair coordinates to the vacant p orbital of AlCl₃, forming a Lewis acid-base complex that subsequently cleaves to yield a carbocation and AlCl₄⁻.

options.label: B
options.text: AlCl₃ deprotonates the alkyl halide to form an alkene.

options.label: C
options.text: A chlorine radical is homolytically abstracted by aluminum.

options.label: D
options.text: Aluminum attacks the methyl carbon via backside SN2 displacement.

questions.correct_answer: A chlorine lone pair coordinates to the vacant p orbital of AlCl₃, forming a Lewis acid-base complex that subsequently cleaves to yield a carbocation and AlCl₄⁻.
questions.explanation: AlCl₃ acts as an electrophilic Lewis acid, coordinating the halogen lone pair and weakening the C-Cl bond for heterolytic cleavage.

questions.question: How does the pKa difference between reactants and products dictate the equilibrium position of an acid-base mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: Equilibrium always favors the side with smaller molecules regardless of pKa.

options.label: B
options.text: Equilibrium favors the stronger acid to maximize heat release.

options.label: C
options.text: Equilibrium always favors the side with the weaker acid (higher pKa) and weaker conjugate base, with Keq = 10^(pKa_product_acid - pKa_reactant_acid).

options.label: D
options.text: Equilibrium is independent of pKa and depends only on solvent viscosity.

questions.correct_answer: Equilibrium always favors the side with the weaker acid (higher pKa) and weaker conjugate base, with Keq = 10^(pKa_product_acid - pKa_reactant_acid).
questions.explanation: Acid-base equilibria thermodynamically shift toward the more stable, lower-energy conjugate acid-base pair (higher pKa).

questions.question: Why is p-nitrophenol (pKa 7.15) much more acidic than phenol (pKa 9.95)?

options.label: A
options.text: p-Nitrophenol undergoes rapid tautomerization to an aliphatic ketone.

options.label: B
options.text: The nitro group donates electron density into the aromatic ring.

options.label: C
options.text: The nitro group physically blocks base access to the phenoxide oxygen.

options.label: D
options.text: The para nitro group provides an additional resonance contributor that delocalizes the phenoxide negative charge directly onto the electronegative nitro oxygens.

questions.correct_answer: The para nitro group provides an additional resonance contributor that delocalizes the phenoxide negative charge directly onto the electronegative nitro oxygens.
questions.explanation: Direct resonance conjugation between the phenoxide oxygen and the para nitro group provides extra stabilization to the conjugate base.

questions.question: Why is methanol (pKa 15.5) slightly more acidic than tert-butanol (pKa 18.0) in aqueous solution?

options.label: A
options.text: The methyl group is more electron-withdrawing than three methyl groups.

options.label: B
options.text: Methanol has more hyperconjugation than tert-butanol.

options.label: C
options.text: The unhindered methoxide anion is more effectively solvated and stabilized by hydrogen-bonding water networks than the sterically bulky tert-butoxide.

options.label: D
options.text: tert-Butoxide is an aromatic anion.

questions.correct_answer: The unhindered methoxide anion is more effectively solvated and stabilized by hydrogen-bonding water networks than the sterically bulky tert-butoxide.
questions.explanation: Steric hindrance in tert-butoxide impedes solvent molecules from closely coordinating and solvating the negative charge.

options.text: The larger 3p orbital of sulfur delocalizes and stabilizes negative charge density over a larger volume than the compact 2p orbital of oxygen.

options.label: B
options.text: Ethanethiol undergoes rapid resonance delocalization into the ethyl chain.

options.label: C
options.text: Ethanol forms stronger intramolecular hydrogen bonds that trap the proton.

options.label: D
options.text: Sulfur is more electronegative than oxygen on the Pauling scale.

questions.correct_answer: The larger 3p orbital of sulfur delocalizes and stabilizes negative charge density over a larger volume than the compact 2p orbital of oxygen.
questions.explanation: Down a column in the periodic table, atomic size dominates over electronegativity: larger polarizable orbitals stabilize conjugate base anions.

questions.question: What mechanistic factor accounts for the ~11 pKa unit acidity difference between acetic acid (pKa 4.76) and ethanol (pKa 16)?

options.label: A
options.text: The acetate conjugate base delocalizes negative charge equally across two electronegative oxygen atoms via resonance, whereas ethoxide localizes charge on one oxygen.

options.label: B
options.text: Acetic acid has stronger inductive electron donation from its methyl group.

options.label: C
options.text: Ethanol undergoes spontaneous homolytic cleavage in water.

options.label: D
options.text: Acetate anion is stabilized by aromaticity.

questions.correct_answer: The acetate conjugate base delocalizes negative charge equally across two electronegative oxygen atoms via resonance, whereas ethoxide localizes charge on one oxygen.
questions.explanation: Resonance delocalization of the negative charge over two equivalent oxygen atoms provides massive stabilization to the carboxylate conjugate base.

questions.question: How does a trifluoromethyl group (-CF₃) mechanistically decrease the pKa of an adjacent carboxylic acid?

options.label: A
options.text: The CF₃ group acts as a Brønsted base that absorbs excess protons.

options.label: B
options.text: Strongly electronegative fluorine atoms pull σ-electron density through inductive polarization, dispersing negative charge away from the carboxylate group.

options.label: C
options.text: Fluorine donates lone pairs into the carboxylate π system via resonance.

options.label: D
options.text: Fluorine forms covalent bonds directly with incoming hydronium ions.

questions.correct_answer: Strongly electronegative fluorine atoms pull σ-electron density through inductive polarization, dispersing negative charge away from the carboxylate group.
questions.explanation: Inductive electron withdrawal through σ bonds stabilizes the conjugate base anion, lowering the energy barrier for proton loss.

questions.question: Why is acetylene (sp, pKa 25) significantly more acidic than ethylene (sp², pKa 44) and ethane (sp³, pKa 50)?

options.label: A
options.text: The sp orbital has a larger volume than sp³ orbitals.

options.label: B
options.text: Acetylene undergoes resonance delocalization upon losing a proton.

options.label: C
options.text: The sp hybrid orbital of the acetylide carbanion has 50% s-character, holding the lone pair electrons closer to the positively charged nucleus.

options.label: D
options.text: The triple bond creates an internal dipole that repels protons.

questions.correct_answer: The sp hybrid orbital of the acetylide carbanion has 50% s-character, holding the lone pair electrons closer to the positively charged nucleus.
questions.explanation: Higher s-character means electrons reside closer to the nucleus, significantly enhancing carbanion conjugate base stability.

questions.question: What is the mechanistic fate of sodium ethoxide (NaOEt) when added to pure water?

options.label: A
options.text: Ethoxide is oxidized to acetic acid by dissolved oxygen.

options.label: B
options.text: Ethoxide rapidly and quantitatively abstracts a proton from water to form ethanol and hydroxide ion (OH⁻), the strongest base that can exist in water.

options.label: C
options.text: Ethoxide remains unreacted as free C₂H₅O⁻ ions.

options.label: D
options.text: Ethoxide decomposes to ethylene gas and water.

questions.correct_answer: Ethoxide rapidly and quantitatively abstracts a proton from water to form ethanol and hydroxide ion (OH⁻), the strongest base that can exist in water.
questions.explanation: Any base stronger than hydroxide is leveled by water, converting completely to the solvent's conjugate base (OH⁻).

questions.question: Why is p-nitrophenol (pKa 7.15) much more acidic than phenol (pKa 9.95)?

options.label: A
options.text: The nitro group physically blocks base access to the phenoxide oxygen.

options.label: B
options.text: The nitro group donates electron density into the aromatic ring.

options.label: C
options.text: p-Nitrophenol undergoes rapid tautomerization to an aliphatic ketone.

options.label: D
options.text: The para nitro group provides an additional resonance contributor that delocalizes the phenoxide negative charge directly onto the electronegative nitro oxygens.

questions.correct_answer: The para nitro group provides an additional resonance contributor that delocalizes the phenoxide negative charge directly onto the electronegative nitro oxygens.
questions.explanation: Direct resonance conjugation between the phenoxide oxygen and the para nitro group provides extra stabilization to the conjugate base.

questions.question: Why is methanol (pKa 15.5) slightly more acidic than tert-butanol (pKa 18.0) in aqueous solution?

options.label: A
options.text: The methyl group is more electron-withdrawing than three methyl groups.

options.label: B
options.text: Methanol has more hyperconjugation than tert-butanol.

options.label: C
options.text: The unhindered methoxide anion is more effectively solvated and stabilized by hydrogen-bonding water networks than the sterically bulky tert-butoxide.

options.label: D
options.text: tert-Butoxide is an aromatic anion.

questions.correct_answer: The unhindered methoxide anion is more effectively solvated and stabilized by hydrogen-bonding water networks than the sterically bulky tert-butoxide.
questions.explanation: Steric hindrance in tert-butoxide impedes solvent molecules from closely coordinating and solvating the negative charge.

questions.question: What is the universal curved-arrow sequence in a single-step Brønsted acid-base reaction?

options.label: A
options.text: One arrow from the base lone pair to the acidic proton, and a second arrow from the H-A σ bond onto the conjugate base atom A.

options.label: B
options.text: One arrow from the acidic proton to the base lone pair.

options.label: C
options.text: An arrow breaking the base into two ions.

options.label: D
options.text: Two arrows transferring protons in opposite directions simultaneously.

questions.correct_answer: One arrow from the base lone pair to the acidic proton, and a second arrow from the H-A σ bond onto the conjugate base atom A.
questions.explanation: The electron pair of the base forms a new bond to H⁺, while the bonding pair in H-A is transferred entirely to atom A.

questions.question: What is the first elementary step when AlCl₃ reacts with 2-chloro-2-methylpropane?

options.label: A
options.text: AlCl₃ deprotonates the alkyl halide to form an alkene.

options.label: B
options.text: A chlorine lone pair coordinates to the vacant p orbital of AlCl₃, forming a Lewis acid-base complex that subsequently cleaves to yield a carbocation and AlCl₄⁻.

options.label: C
options.text: Aluminum attacks the methyl carbon via backside SN2 displacement.

options.label: D
options.text: A chlorine radical is homolytically abstracted by aluminum.

questions.correct_answer: A chlorine lone pair coordinates to the vacant p orbital of AlCl₃, forming a Lewis acid-base complex that subsequently cleaves to yield a carbocation and AlCl₄⁻.
questions.explanation: AlCl₃ acts as an electrophilic Lewis acid, coordinating the halogen lone pair and weakening the C-Cl bond for heterolytic cleavage.

questions.question: How does the pKa difference between reactants and products dictate the equilibrium position of an acid-base mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: Equilibrium always favors the side with the weaker acid (higher pKa) and weaker conjugate base, with Keq = 10^(pKa_product_acid - pKa_reactant_acid).

options.label: B
options.text: Equilibrium always favors the side with smaller molecules regardless of pKa.

options.label: C
options.text: Equilibrium favors the stronger acid to maximize heat release.

options.label: D
options.text: Equilibrium is independent of pKa and depends only on solvent viscosity.

questions.correct_answer: Equilibrium always favors the side with the weaker acid (higher pKa) and weaker conjugate base, with Keq = 10^(pKa_product_acid - pKa_reactant_acid).
questions.explanation: Acid-base equilibria thermodynamically shift toward the more stable, lower-energy conjugate acid-base pair (higher pKa).
